title: Great Wall of China
content: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states and Imperial China to protect against nomadic groups from the Eurasian Steppe.

title: Great Wall of China
content: Contrary to a popular myth, the Great Wall is not visible to the unaided human eye from low Earth orbit, and it is certainly not visible from the Moon.

title: Lightning
content: Lightning is a sudden electrostatic discharge that occurs during a thunderstorm. This discharge happens between electrically charged regions of a cloud, between two clouds, or between a cloud and the ground.

title: Lightning
content: Tall, isolated structures such as skyscrapers and radio masts are often struck by lightning many times during a single storm, so the saying that lightning never strikes the same place twice is false.

title: Speed of light
content: The speed of light in a vacuum, commonly denoted c, is a universal physical constant exactly equal to 299,792,458 metres per second.

title: Speed of light
content: According to the theory of special relativity, c is the upper limit for the speed at which conventional matter, energy, or any information can travel through space.

title: Moon
content: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite. It orbits Earth at an average distance of about 384,400 kilometres.

title: Moon
content: The far side of the Moon is not permanently dark; both the near and far sides receive roughly equal amounts of sunlight over a lunar day, even though the far side always faces away from Earth.

title: Goldfish
content: The goldfish is a freshwater fish in the family Cyprinidae and one of the most commonly kept aquarium fish.

title: Goldfish
content: Studies have shown that goldfish have a memory span of at least several months and can be trained to respond to cues, contradicting the myth of a three-second memory.

title: Mount Everest
content: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas. Its summit reaches 8,849 metres above sea level.

title: Amazon rainforest
content: The Amazon rainforest is a moist broadleaf tropical rainforest in the Amazon biome that covers most of the Amazon basin of South America.
